reasons: No tests are visible in the packet.
The commercial use setting is not enforced here.
The list of policy files is written by hand, so a new file is ignored until added.

terms.meaning: The legal permission that says what a user may do with data.
Something new made from the source data, such as a summary or a calculation.
Converting text into numbers so it can be searched by meaning.
Using data to teach a computer model, which some licences forbid.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and policy files
sections.what: States that this module covers data licences only, not software, media, trademark or athlete image rights. Brings in five source policy files.
sections.why: Keeps each source's licence in its own reviewable file.
sections.watch_out: The five files are listed by hand, so a new policy file is ignored until it is added here.

sections.name: rightsPolicy, RightsPolicy, RightsAction
sections.title: Shape of a licence record
sections.what: Defines what each policy file must say: source id, display name, allowed uses for storing, showing, deriving, embedding, training and video, commercial use, territories, attribution, prototype status and notes. Unknown fields are refused.
sections.why: Makes licence terms explicit and checkable.
sections.watch_out: The commercial use field is recorded but no check in this file uses it.

sections.name: FIELD
sections.title: Mapping uses to licence flags
sections.what: Matches each kind of use to its flag in a policy.
sections.why: Lets one check handle every kind of use.
sections.watch_out: A new kind of use must be added to both this map and the list of uses.

sections.name: RightsError
sections.title: Error for refused use
sections.what: Defines the error raised when a use is refused, naming the source, the use and the reason.
sections.why: Makes refusals easy to spot in logs and tests.
sections.watch_out: Code that catches this error should not ignore it, or the refusal is lost.

sections.name: POLICIES, RightsContext
sections.title: Loading and checking licence records
sections.what: Checks all five policy files when the module loads and stores them by source id. Defines the context that says whether prototype data is allowed.
sections.why: A bad licence file stops the app at startup rather than causing a silent error later.
sections.watch_out: Two policies with the same source id overwrite each other without any warning.

sections.name: listPolicies
sections.title: Listing all licences
sections.what: Returns every licence sorted by display name.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app list sources, such as for credit lines.

sections.name: getPolicy
sections.title: Looking up one licence
sections.what: Returns the licence for one source id, or nothing if the id is unknown.
sections.why: Lets the app show a source's attribution text.
sections.watch_out: An unknown id returns nothing, so every caller must handle that case.

sections.name: checkRight
sections.title: Deciding if a use is allowed
sections.what: Answers yes or no for one use of one source. Refuses unknown sources, refuses prototype-only sources unless prototype data is on, and refuses when the matching flag is off.
sections.why: The safe default: anything not clearly allowed is refused.
sections.watch_out: The prototype setting comes from whoever calls this, so a live deployment that switches it on opens prototype sources.

sections.name: assertRight
sections.title: Stopping a refused use
sections.what: Runs the same check and throws the refusal error if the use is not allowed. Otherwise returns the policy.
sections.why: Lets callers stop before storing, showing or embedding data.
sections.watch_out: A caller that catches the error and carries on defeats the protection.

summary: The licence check for data sources: it decides which uses of each source are allowed, and refuses anything not clearly permitted.
purpose: It stops the app storing, showing or deriving data from a source whose licence does not allow it.
why: Licence terms differ by source, and keeping them in files with a single check keeps the rules visible and reviewable.
how: It loads and checks five policy files when the module starts, storing each by source id. The check function refuses unknown sources, refuses prototype-only sources unless prototype data is on, and refuses any use whose flag is off. The assert function does the same check and throws an error when refused.
inputs: A source id, the kind of use requested, and whether prototype data is allowed.
outputs: A yes or no answer with its policy, a list of policies, one policy by id, or an error for a refused use.
risks: The commercial use setting is recorded but never checked. If prototype data is switched on in a live deployment, prototype sources become usable.
debug: If a use is refused, read the reason: it names the missing policy, the prototype setting, or the flag. Check the policy file for the source.
